title: the OC Hypercar's graphics pass, outside and inside
lensAText: a sceptical automotive art director for a premium driving game. Look at every before/after image the builder cites with the Read tool and at the owner's wheel references (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/owner/hyper-wheel/wheel-ref-1.webp, -2, -3), then build dist/artifact.html yourself and take your own frames in ONE short Playwright script: the OC Hypercar from the chase and hood cameras on the freeway by day and at night (1280x720), the seat view (setCam('cockpit')) at 390x844 (phone viewport copy, isMobile, hasTouch, DPR 3) and 1280x720 by day and night, and the garage view. Judge: is the outside now a clear step up (clean deep paint with unbroken reflections and no dark patches or faceting, deliberate two-tone edges, shut lines, carbon weave, crisp lights, grounded by a contact shadow, the same silhouette)? Is the cockpit a premium hypercar interior with a clearer view of the road (slimmer pillars, sculpted fender tops, Alcantara and stitching, carbon, ambient lines), and does the wheel follow the owner's references (navy Alcantara with blue stitching, carbon sections, silver spokes, rounded-hex centre, lit 12 o'clock line) while keeping the OC mark? Our own design, no real brand marks, no emblem from the reference pictures? Are the other four cars unchanged? Drive 60 s in the seat view steering to full lock both ways at 390x844 DPR 3 and watch for clipping, z-fighting, flicker, shimmer or stutter; check the builder's frame-time table against one short measurement of your own (CDP CPU throttle 4).
brief: THE OWNER (2026-11-15 ~3:25 PM PT): "let's also start fixing the graphics for the OC hyper car both outside and inside the car" (and earlier, Nov 11: "make sure graphics are insane for both the steering wheel and characters and ... no laggy graphics or glitchy 1st person POV"). HEAD is 572111a (origin/claude/sport-wheel: the live v15 game plus the reviewed dashboard and wheel centre, which go live in drop 3 tonight); branch claude/hyper-gfx. Read PROJECT_OC_HYPERCAR.md (the M1/M1b/M2 notes: the body is a procedural model in src/preview/car-shape.ts, car-body.ts, car-kit.ts, car-mats.ts, car-tex.ts, car.ts, oc-mark.ts; the cockpit in src/preview/cockpit.ts, wheel-sport.ts, car-dash.ts; the game wiring in src/game/vehicle/PlayerCar.ts) and PROJECT_OC_STYLE_GUIDE.md first. The owner's reference sheet (scratchpad/ref/hypercar-reference.png) was lost in a machine reset; use the figures recorded in PROJECT_OC_HYPERCAR.md and the M1b renders as the shape to keep (this is a GRAPHICS pass, not a redesign: same silhouette and proportions). (A) OUTSIDE (garage, chase, hood and hero cameras): make it read as a premium real-time hypercar: (1) paint: a deep clear-coat silver with fine metallic flake and crisp, unbroken reflections (fix the stretched dark patches and blotches on the bonnet and front fenders seen in M1b's hero, whose cause was never traced; no faceting: smooth normals or more stations where needed); (2) the two-tone: the gloss-black areas with clean, deliberate edges (no ragged patches or blotchy masks; the side triangles and fender scoops should read as designed shapes); (3) shut lines and panel gaps (doors, bonnet, engine cover) as thin dark lines; (4) carbon fibre with a visible weave under clear coat on the splitter, diffuser, side blades, wing and mirrors; (5) the glass/canopy dark tinted with real reflections; (6) lights: the headlamp blades and the rear bar crisp and emissive with a subtle bloom on HD/Ultra, LED detail in the lamp sockets; (7) underbody contact shadow / ambient occlusion so it sits on the road; (8) a few hero details: mesh grilles in the intakes, the exhaust exits, a fine aero vane set in the diffuser, mirror stalks. The road wheels' rims, tyres and calipers live in src/preview/car-wheel.ts, which another session owns: do NOT edit it; you may change only how the car's own materials are passed to it if that is already a public option. (B) INSIDE (the seat view the player drives in, phone 390x844 and desktop): today the view shows a huge black diagonal A-pillar/canopy frame over the top-left, plain grey fender humps over the dash, flat featureless dash and door panels and a blank grey console. Make it a premium hypercar cockpit, keeping the player's view of the road clear: slimmer A-pillars and canopy frame (or a frame that reads as sculpted carbon, not a black slab) that hide less of the road; the fender tops seen over the dash as sculpted silver forms with clean reflections; the dash top in navy Alcantara with blue double stitching; a carbon tub and centre console with satin-silver trim lines, gloss-black touch panels with thin icons, ice-blue ambient light lines; sculpted door cards; the mirror housings in carbon. THE WHEEL (owner's references, Nov 11: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/owner/hyper-wheel/wheel-ref-1.webp, -2, -3: look at them): deep navy Alcantara grips with bright blue double stitching, gloss carbon top and bottom sections with thin silver trim lines, a lit ice-blue line at 12 o'clock and down the lower spoke, satin silver/titanium sculpted spokes and paddles, a rounded-hexagon centre in navy leather/Alcantara with a blue stitched edge, gloss-black touch panels with thin icons and small knurled metal rollers on the upper spokes; keep the hub lane's centre structure and badge cup; the badge stays the current OC mark (the owner's new emblems are not picked yet; the emblems drawn in those pictures must NOT be used); the rim path and grips where the hands hold it (GRIP 32/148 deg) unchanged; the dials, thumb pads, paddles, shift lights and the new cluster keep working. RULES: our own design only (no real brand's logo, name or copied shape); the other four cars (Rossini GT, Corsa, Brio, Vela E) must be UNCHANGED: hash their geometry and material settings against HEAD as M1b did (tests/out/preview/m1b/hash/) and show pixel-identical renders; do NOT edit src/preview/spec.ts, hands*, car-wheel.ts, Physics.ts, src/onfoot/*; Low stays cheap for phones (simpler interior and materials on Low), HD and Ultra get the full detail; stay inside the hypercar's budget in PROJECT_OC_HYPERCAR.md section 10 (40 draw calls / 260,000 triangles high, 36 / 135,000 phone) unless a small, stated increase on HD/Ultra buys a visible step (never on Low); no per-frame allocation; mipmaps and anisotropy on every new texture (no shimmer); no z-fighting or flicker. SMOOTHNESS: measure a 60 s seat-view drive with steering to full lock both ways, phone profile (390x844, DPR 3, isMobile, CDP CPU throttle 4) and desktop 1280x720, as 3 alternating base/ours pairs (base = a clean build of 572111a in a temporary detached worktree under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/tmp-base, node_modules symlinked from /home/user/Claude/tsu-live/top-speed-ultra/node_modules, removed afterwards); PASS = draw calls and triangles within the stated budget, median p50 within +10 %, median p95 within +10 % or inside the base's own spread, no heap growth. PROVE: npx tsc --noEmit (both configs); npm run build (one owner-test mark); npm test -- --only=boot,phone,render (each run under 20 minutes; split render with --check if needed); before (572111a) and after renders into tests/out/hyper-gfx/: test-car.ts views hero (the sheet's camera), hero-night, front, rear, rear 3/4, side, top, wheel close-up and the interior/seat view, plus in-game frames: chase and hood on the freeway by day and at night (1280x720), and the seat view at 390x844 (phone viewport copy, DPR 3) and 1280x720, day and night; a close-up of the steering wheel beside the owner's three wheel references. Look at every image you cite. Log it in PROJECT_OC_HYPERCAR.md (a new 'G1 graphics pass' row) and PROJECT_OC_PROGRESS.md.
